rules.rule: Participe en adjectif : -ED = sens passif (the quoted price, the attached file) ; -ING = qui provoque (encouraging results)
rules.example: the quoted price ; encouraging results

rules.rule: Collocations : comply WITH, in accordance WITH, adhere TO, eligible FOR
rules.example: comply with the regulations ; in accordance with standards

rules.rule: SUBJONCTIF : recommend / request / suggest / insist / it is essential that + sujet + BASE VERBALE (sans -s, sans to)
rules.example: requested that Ms. Lee present ; essential that every employee complete ; that each applicant read

rules.rule: FEWER + pluriel / LESS + indénombrable ; FEW / LITTLE ; SO MANY + pluriel / SO MUCH + indénombrable
rules.example: fewer complaints, very little time, so many applications

rules.rule: EVEN THOUGH / although + phrase (≠ despite + nom)
rules.example: Even though prices rose sharply, sales grew

rules.rule: Some of / most of / all of + INDÉNOMBRABLE → singulier ; + pluriel → pluriel
rules.example: Some of the furniture was damaged / some of the chairs were

rules.rule: Both A and B → verbe PLURIEL
rules.example: Both the report and the budget were approved

rules.rule: each other / one another = l'un l'autre (réciproque)
rules.example: The two companies share resources with each other

rules.rule: Passif au prétérit : was/were + participe passé (le sujet subit l'action)
rules.example: The contract was signed last Friday

rules.rule: Concession : even if / even though / even as (= alors que) ≠ as though, as a result of
rules.example: shuts off even if it has a fully charged battery ; Even as newspapers reported…
Mr. Hobbes is interested in the loan

rules.rule: assemble = monter, assembler ; properly = correctement ; continue
rules.example: homes are fully assembled before being shipped

rules.rule: Partie 6 – phrase à insérer : choisir celle qui se relie à la phrase d'avant / d'après
rules.example: sign up in advance. There is limited seating at this event.
late by more than ninety minutes

rules.rule: strive / plan / aim / decide + TO + verbe
rules.example: we strive to provide

rules.rule: Discours rapporté : will → would (revealed that he would not be teaching)
rules.example: would not be teaching for the upcoming semester

rules.rule: take over = reprendre (un poste, un rôle)
rules.example: take over the role of head chef

rules.rule: conduct = mener, réaliser (a survey, a study, an inspection)
rules.example: conducting a survey

rules.rule: discard = jeter ; in cooperation with ; regarding = about
rules.example: discarded bulbs

rules.rule: Habitude (usually, every day, often) → présent simple (+ s à la 3e pers.)
rules.example: The CEO usually presents the results

rules.rule: Currently / at the moment / now → présent continu
rules.example: Currently, the IT department is upgrading…
the CEO's confidence, their knowledge, the supplier's ability
declare bankruptcy, supporting advances in
suggested moving, recommend checking
the negotiations are nearing completion
rules.rule: It seems / appears that → présent continu

rules.example: a sale in which it offered…
the agency specializes in tours
passengers were stranded at the airport
should be relevant, more cautious
the estimated costs, the most impressive buildings
make the terms agreeable
conveniently located, variously colored
comply with the regulations
the materials outline the schedule
so that its surface doesn't get scratched
rules.rule: so that + phrase / in order to + verbe

rules.example: postponed until next week
For more details, visit…
before agreeing, for the purpose of accommodating
Having joined the gym, …
will have demolished
rules.rule: By the time + futur → will have + pp

rules.example: the judges will choose
None of the attendees was aware
has fallen by 24%
a new manager was appointed
the enclosed contract
a test drive

rules.rule: Date passée (last…, ago, in 2019) → prétérit ; since / for / yet / so far → present perfect
rules.example: opened in 2019 / has worked since 2021
